show.title: Proko - Drawing Basics
show.creator: Stan Prokopenko
show.plot: Stan Prokopenko's foundation course in drawing: 185 lessons across eight chapters covering lines, shapes, perspective, values and edges. The claim it opens on is that anyone can learn to draw the same way anyone can learn to speak, because drawing is a visual language. There are no prerequisites — this course is the prerequisite.

lessons.title: Learning How to Draw
lessons.plot: Stan opens the course with its central claim: anyone can learn to draw, just as anyone can learn to speak — drawing is a visual language and two-year-olds manage the spoken one. The course is meant to be refreshingly simple, fun and enlightening, teaching the fundamental concepts for drawing anything from reference or from imagination.

lessons.title: Intro to Drawing Basics
lessons.plot: A walkthrough of how the course is structured. Stan lays out what the fundamentals of visual language will let you do: design characters, render them with confident lines and perspective, and shade forms so they read as three-dimensional.

lessons.title: Project - Get Your Tools and Start Playing
lessons.plot: The first assignment. Before anything else you need tools — go and get some, then spend time playing with them rather than trying to produce a finished drawing.

lessons.title: Ultimate Guide to Sketchbooks and Paper
lessons.plot: A beginner's guide to sketchbooks and paper with lotsa juicy info about paper types, texture, weight, archivability and most importantly, how to avoid the common mental pitfall of sketchbooking.

lessons.title: Ultimate Guide to Pencils and Erasers
lessons.plot: A beginner's guide to pencils and erasers! A breakdown of the many different pencil and eraser options out there. I'll go over the different types, how they each differ from one another, the best way to hold them, and the most effective way to use them.

lessons.title: Sharpening 6 Types of Drawing Pencils
lessons.plot: How to sharpen six different kinds of drawing pencil, and what each shape of point is good for.

lessons.title: Project - Simplify from Observation
lessons.plot: Before moving on to Lines, an opportunity to actually draw. The assignment is to simplify a subject down to its shapes, values and edges — level 1 is a pear, level 2 a portrait. The reference photos are filed next to this episode.

lessons.title: Demo - Simplify Pear from Observation
lessons.plot: Stan works through the level 1 assignment himself, simplifying a pear from observation into shapes, values and edges.

lessons.title: Demo - Simplify Portrait from Observation
lessons.plot: Stan works through the level 2 assignment himself, simplifying a portrait from observation into shapes, values and edges.

lessons.title: Critique - Simplify Pear from Observation
lessons.plot: A clip taken from the premium critique of the Drawing Basics course. The assignment was to simplify a pear or a portrait down to its shapes, values, and edges. In this critique, I break down some of the common issues I saw students have with their shape design. I'll give you advice and talk about proportion, asymmetry, and improving your shadow shape design.

lessons.title: Critique - Simplify Portrait from Observation
lessons.plot: A critique clip from the level 2 Drawing Basics project on simplifying portraits using shapes, values, and edges.

lessons.title: Warmup - Mushrooms
lessons.plot: A fun exercise to warm up your hand and get you comfortable with drawing fluid lines. While doodling with my son, he asked me to draw a Mario mushroom, and I realized it's a perfect way to practice ellipses.

lessons.title: Intro to Lines
lessons.plot: There is an endless number of ways to use lines as an artist, so let's jump in and take a look at the basics.

lessons.title: Project - Simplify to CSI
lessons.plot: Here's a project to help you avoid chicken scratch. We're going to simplify our drawings to C curves, S curves, and straight lines.

lessons.title: 2 Week Drawing Challenge
lessons.plot: Challenge yourself to draw every day for two weeks.

lessons.title: Demo - Simplify Snail and Boots to CSI
lessons.plot: In this demo, I'll show you how I would approach the level 1 CSI drawings.

lessons.title: Demo - Simplify Camel and Skull to CSI
lessons.plot: In this demo, I'll show you how I would approach the level 2 CSI drawings.

lessons.title: Critique - Simplify to CSI
lessons.plot: Let's take a look at your "Simplify to CSI" submissions!

lessons.title: How to Draw Confident Lines - The Tapered Stroke
lessons.plot: Master the Tapered Stroke for confident line quality in your sketches! Learn how to construct complex shapes & add energy to your loose sketches.

lessons.title: Searching Lines
lessons.plot: Searching Lines, 3 levels of looseness, and their practical applications.

lessons.title: Project - Learning to Sketch from Observation
lessons.plot: In this project, we'll start learning how to sketch using simple loose lines.

lessons.title: Project - Learning to Sketch from Imagination
lessons.plot: This is our first stop on the path to drawing from imagination.

lessons.title: Drawing from Imagination Cramps
lessons.plot: Why drawing from imagination is important for artists, when to start, and overcoming the emotional challenges.

lessons.title: Demo - Learning to Sketch from Observation
lessons.plot: In this lesson, I walk you through each step of my process for sketching all 3 of the "Learning to Sketch from Observation" reference images.

lessons.title: Demo - Learning to Sketch from Imagination
lessons.plot: I demonstrate the sketching from imagination project. From studying the reference, to explorations, to final sketch.

lessons.title: Critique - Learning to Sketch from Observation
lessons.plot: In this lesson, I'll look over your sketches from observation and address the common mistakes.

lessons.title: Critique - Learning to Sketch from Imagination
lessons.plot: Reviewing the common mistakes and standout assignments from the "Learning to Sketch from Imagination" projects.

lessons.title: Warmups to Improve Line Quality
lessons.plot: In this lesson, I show you 5 line quality warm-ups that you can practice to improve your line control.

lessons.title: 6 Habits for Good Line Quality
lessons.plot: Master line quality with 6 key habits: avoid common mistakes, find a comfortable speed, follow-through, ghosting, rotate the paper, and use simple strokes.

lessons.title: How to Draw with Line Weight
lessons.plot: In this lesson, we'll learn about the importance of line weight when creating engaging and interesting art.

lessons.title: Project - Organizing Line Weight
lessons.plot: For this project, we're going to design our line quality to be more interesting by practicing organizing the line weight.

lessons.title: Demo - Hierarchy of Importance Line Weight
lessons.plot: In this demo, I show the "hierarchy of importance" method for organizing line weight.

lessons.title: Demo - Light and Shadow Line Weight
lessons.plot: In this demo, I show the "light & shadow" method for organizing line weight.

lessons.title: Demo - Different Ways to Use Line Weight
lessons.plot: Before starting my line weight drawing of shoes, I did some small sketches exploring all the options.

lessons.title: Demo - Depth and Form Line Weight
lessons.plot: In this demo, I show you how to approach the Depth and Form method.

lessons.title: Critique - Organizing Line Weight
lessons.plot: Let's take a look at all your "Organizing Line Weight" projects.

lessons.title: Combining Line Weight
lessons.plot: In this bonus demo, I'll attempt to use ALL 3 line weight methods in the same drawing and show how you can be creative in the way you combine them.

lessons.title: Project - Line Master Studies
lessons.plot: In this new project, you'll practice to improve your line quality by doing master studies!

lessons.title: Demo - Line Master Studies - Jeff Watts
lessons.plot: In this demo, I do a master study of a skull drawing from my instructor Jeff Watts.

lessons.title: Demo - Line Master Studies - Roberto De La Torre
lessons.plot: In this demo, I do a couple master studies from one of my favorite inkers, Roberto De La Torre.

lessons.title: Critique - Line Master Studies
lessons.plot: In this critique, I'll look through your master study assignments and give some advice on how to improve your studies of lines.

lessons.title: Jeff Watts on Line Quality
lessons.plot: In this bonus lesson, we get some great insight on how to effectively use lines from my instructor, Jeff Watts.
